description: Functional validation of the hand (right arm, myoarm_r): passive tenodesis, maximum power grip and lateral pinch, after the protocols of McFarland et al. 2023 (sections III-A, III-B, IV-B, V-A, V-B), reimplemented in MuJoCo by scripts/validate_hand_function.py and checked by tests/test_hand_grip.py, tests/test_hand_pinch.py and tests/test_hand_tenodesis.py. Angles are anatomical (deg): positive is flexion, abduction, radial deviation, forearm pronation, and the script maps them onto each model's joints with a sign (MyoHand: cmc_flexion_r, mp_flexion and ip_flexion are positive in extension). The paper's numbers are model results of the ARMS hand and wrist model unless marked experiment; ARMS is cited only (non-commercial): no file, parameter or coordinate of it is used. Values marked assumed are this reimplementation's choices where the paper's text gives none. Nothing here changes the model; scales_with is none throughout.

mcfarland2023.citation: McFarland et al. A musculoskeletal model of the hand and wrist capable of simulating functional tasks. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 70(5):1424-1435, 2023.
mcfarland2023.access: protocols and results summarised for this validation; the ARMS model (non-commercial) is cited only

odriscoll1992.citation: O'Driscoll SW et al. The relationship between wrist position, grasp size, and grip strength. J Hand Surg Am 17(1):169-177, 1992.

valerocuevas2003.citation: Valero-Cuevas FJ et al. Towards a realistic biomechanical model of the thumb: the choice of kinematic description may be more critical than the solution method or the variability/uncertainty of musculoskeletal parameters. J Biomech 36(7):1019-1030, 2003.

kong2011.citation: Kong et al. 2011, individual finger contributions to gripping (as cited by mcfarland2023).
kong2011.access: cited by mcfarland2023 as similar to its simulated digit shares

lock.note: Locked joints are joint equalities to a constant; the prescribed wrist is the same equality with its constant moved every step. timeconst = 2 x timestep, the stiffest MuJoCo keeps stable. Collisions are off in every scene except the explicit dynamometer pairs.

tenodesis.posture_note: Shoulder neutral, elbow 90 deg, forearm neutral, all muscles at act = 0. Free: MCP, PIP and DIP flexion of digits 2-5. Locked: MCP abduction (0) and the four thumb DOFs (0). Gravity on (in the flexion plane it is negligible with the forearm neutral).
tenodesis.trials: A: hold the wrist at 60 deg flexion for hold_s, then to 60 deg extension at speed_deg_s. B (release): from the end of A, hold at 60 deg extension for hold_s, then to 60 deg flexion. Metrics over each sweep (hold excluded).

targets.note: Average ROM over digits; the index differs most from the other digits, by up to index_gap at a given instant.

tolerances.justification: Model-vs-model targets, so bands, not points. Trial A: every finger joint flexes monotonically as the wrist extends (no reversal beyond 2 deg); MCP ROM per digit 30-85 deg around the paper's 65.2 (a ROM at the 90 deg range means the digit was driven into its flexion limit); mean PIP ROM 5-40 deg (paper 16.1, factor 2.5 either way); DIP 'remained constant': at most 5 deg; inter-digit MCP spread 10-80 deg (paper up to 49.2). Trial B: each MCP ends at least 2 deg, and on average 5 deg, more extended than it started (the digits open as the wrist flexes). Negative controls that must fail: the passive springs removed and the extrinsic slack lengths and fpmax of the passive fit's starting point (the anatomical-parameter values).

grip.posture_note: Shoulder neutral, elbow 90 deg, forearm neutral; wrist held (joint equality) at the posture below; thumb locked at 0 with its intrinsics at 0 and no thumb contact pairs.
grip.wrist_postures_note: Self-selected: 35 deg extension, 7 deg ulnar deviation (paper). The flexed angle is assumed (the mirror of the self-selected extension); the paper's value was not available.

dynamometer.note: Massless elliptical cylinder (convex mesh, 64-gon) in the third-metacarpal body (rigidly attached). 48 mm (Jamar setting II) is the palmar-dorsal span, the paper's value; the 32 mm proximal-distal span is assumed. Axis through the MCP 2 and MCP 5 joint centres; major axis along the palmar normal of the flat third digit; moved palmarly until it touches the palm skin or a flat proximal phalanx; centre_distal_m = -(16 mm + 9 mm), i.e. its distal face one proximal-phalanx skin radius proximal of MCP 3, so the proximal phalanges flexed about 90 deg lie along it (assumed; grip force depends strongly on this placement, see the wiki page).

contact.note: Paper: skin E 12.3 MPa, Poisson 0.48; dynamometer E 1.75 GPa, Poisson 0.43; friction 0.29. MuJoCo has no elastic moduli: friction 0.29 is used as given; the stiffest stable soft contact (timeconst 2 x timestep, critically damped, impedance 0.95 -> 0.99 over 1 mm) stands in for the near-rigid dynamometer against loaded skin. A Hertz line contact with the paper's moduli (E* about 16 MPa) indents about 0.1-1 mm at these loads; the protocol reports the largest penetration, which stays below 1 mm. At a quasi-static grip the force is set by the muscles and the contact geometry, not by the contact stiffness.

closing.note: Every evaluation starts from the hand closed on the dynamometer by FDS, FDP and the finger intrinsics at 0.3 for 0.5 s from the flat hand (assumed).

settled.note: Reported next to the eval_s grip, not tested: the optimum's levels held for settle_s from the same closed hand (force and lock moments averaged over the last average_s, as for eval_s), with the relative change of the grip since check_s. The optimisation and the tolerances use the paper's eval_s; at fixed levels the grip keeps changing well after it (see the wiki page).

grip.activation: Paper: 12 independent levels (wrist muscles, extrinsic thumb, EIP, EDM), one shared level each for the FDS, FDP and EDC slips, the finger intrinsics at 1 (ARMS: 14; MyoHand: 12, RI/LU_RB/UI_UB of digits 2-5), the thumb intrinsics at 0; activations set directly (steady state). Grip: contact force of the proximal and middle phalanges on the dynamometer, perpendicular to its axis (sum of magnitudes); distal contacts act but are not counted.
grip.balance_note: Penalty on wrist motion, implemented as a penalty on the moment the wrist lock has to supply (the wrist would move without it): grip - 1000 N/(N m) x |lock moment| (L1). 'held' runs drop the penalty (wrist rigidly held).

status.normative_male_20_30_N: normative range as reported by mcfarland2023

tolerances.justification: Grip within the experimental mean +- 1 SD (O'Driscoll 1992). Digit shares within 12 percentage points of the paper's (its own ARMS shares differ from Kong 2011 by several points). Neutral and flexed wrists each lose 20-80 % against the self-selected posture (paper 41 and 46 %), and the flexed loses at least as much as the neutral. With the balance penalty the wrist lock supplies at most 0.5 N m. Negative control: the flexors (FDS, FDP) at half their peak force must fall below the band.

cached.note: Optimum found by scripts/validate_hand_function.py for each model; tests/test_hand_grip.py re-evaluates the entry whose fingerprint matches the model (actuator and position counts, passive_* spring tendons present, damping of mcp2_flexion_r, fpmax of EDC3, palm pad thickness, fpmax of OP, stiffness of the EDC4-EDC5 junctura) and, with MYO_SIM_SLOW=1, re-optimises. The optimum depends on the model: the levels that balance the wrist of one leave a lock moment on the other.

pinch.posture_note: Paper (lateral pinch): thumb CMC 15 deg extension and 20 deg adduction, MP 20 deg flexion, IP 40 deg flexion; wrist 0/0; fingers locked (at 0). Mapping onto MyoHand: MyoHand's thumb comes from the same MoBL-ARMS (Holzbaur 2005) kinematics; the anatomical sense of each joint was read from muscle actions at the posture (FPL, OP and the thenar muscles flex the CMC with negative cmc_flexion_r, EPL and EPB extend it with positive; APB abducts with positive cmc_abduction_r, AdP and EPL adduct with negative; FPL flexes the MP and IP with negative angles). So cmc_flexion_r = +15, cmc_abduction_r = -20, mp_flexion = -20, ip_flexion = -40 deg (joint values). Both models' CMC angles are measured from their own zero, which the paper's text does not relate to anatomical landmarks: this mapping is the largest uncertainty of the protocol (see the wiki page).
pinch.method: Static, on the four thumb DOFs: the tip (the point of the distal-phalanx collision geometry farthest from the IP joint) presses on a sensor fixed to the ground. J^T F = tau(a) with J the 3 x 4 tip Jacobian needs tau along J's null space to vanish; F is maximised along the palmar normal of the distal phalanx (its tip's motion under IP flexion) with the off-axis part at most off_axis_max of it, over the extrinsic thumb muscles and the thumb intrinsics (OP, AdP, FPB, APB) in [0, 1] (SLSQP, deterministic restarts). The optimum is checked in MuJoCo with the sensor reaction applied at the tip (residual thumb moment).

status.normative_N: reported only; no model reaches it

tolerances.justification: In vivo mean +- 1 SD (Valero-Cuevas 2003). Negative control: without the thenar muscles AdP, FPB and APB no force meets the off-axis limit.
